topic: Dallas-Fort Worth (TX) and Miami / South Florida as candidate remote-served markets for Integra Dental Design (Bellevue, WA): dentist and lab supply, full-arch/DSO demand structure, state lab regulation, tax and entity costs, labor, real estate, flights and parcel logistics; conclusion on obtainable accounts in 12 months
summary:
Bottom line: neither Dallas-Fort Worth nor South Florida gives a Bellevue lab a structural edge over local labs or national mail-order labs. Of the two, DFW is the less-bad option, and only as a lab-to-lab milling and equipment-dealer play; South Florida has no structural case and should be deprioritized behind Southern California, where Integra already has accounts and family presence.

FACTS. (1) Regulation is asymmetric. Texas Occupations Code 266.151 requires a registration certificate for any person who "provide[s] or offer[s] to provide dental laboratory services," and 266.153 covers "each dental laboratory doing business in this state"; nothing in ch. 266, 22 TAC ch. 116, or TSBDE's "Do I Need a Dental Laboratory Registration" chart exempts an out-of-state lab, and 266.102(b)(5)(D)-(E) gives the Board rulemaking power over prescriptions referred to out-of-state labs. Registration is $125 initial / $136 annual (TSBDE 2022 application form; current schedule page would not render) but requires a Certified Dental Technician "employed by and working on the premises" at least 30 hours/week (22 TAC 116.5) and a jurisprudence assessment. The brief does not say whether Integra employs a CDT; if it does not, Texas is a compliance problem before it is a sales problem. Florida is the opposite: Fla. Stat. 466.032(5)(d)2 states an out-of-state lab serving a Florida dentist "is not required to register"; voluntary registration costs $200 (Board page) with 18 CE hours biennially. Both states exempt dental prostheses from sales tax (Tex. Tax Code 151.313(a)(5) "dental, or prosthetic device"; Fla. Stat. 212.08(2)(a) "dentures... prosthetic and orthopedic appliances," Rule 12A-1.021). Foreign-LLC registration is $750 in Texas (BOC 4.152(3) via 4.154) plus an annual franchise report (no tax below the $2.65M 2026-27 threshold) and $125 plus $138.75/yr in Florida.

(2) Lab supply is the decisive asymmetry. Census CBP 2023 (via two secondary tabulations) shows Florida with 424 dental-lab establishments, second in the nation, versus Texas 277 and Washington 175. BLS OEWS May 2023 shows the Miami metro with 800 dental lab technicians at a location quotient of 1.31 versus DFW 670 at 0.75 (Texas statewide LQ 0.57, Florida 1.12). South Florida is over-supplied with lab capacity relative to the U.S.; DFW is under-supplied and already imports lab work. A directory count (poidata, June 2026) lists 97 labs in Miami and 42 in Hialeah alone. South Florida labs advertise 48-hour zirconia with free pickup across Miami-Dade and Broward (Rivfor), 24-hour rush (Esthetic Dental Laboratory), 3-day standard (Vita), and same-day printed immediate-load arches for Broward/Palm Beach surgeons (Dental Lab Miami). DFW labs are fewer and advertise slower service (American Dental Laboratory 10 days in lab; Luna Labs 5-7 business days).

(3) Dentist counts are comparable. Texas DSHS (Sept 2020): Dallas 1,678, Tarrant 1,093, Collin 884, Denton 450 (4,105). Florida DOH 2019-20 survey: Miami-Dade 1,783, Broward 1,476, Palm Beach 1,110 (4,369, with some dual-county reporting). Newer official counts exist (DSHS 2024 dashboard; FL 2023-24 report) but were not machine-readable.

(4) Demand structure works against a remote full-arch lab. Most full-arch centers in both metros run in-house labs (DFW: Advanced Dentistry, ARCHPOINT, Texas Implant & Dental Center, Forte, The Dental Implant Place at 98% in-house, Innate, Dallas All-on-4 Center; South Florida: Nuvia Miami, OneSolution, Done In One, In A Day Smile, Smiland, Boca Dental, Art Dental Studio). They are overflow or titanium-bar targets at best. DFW is a DSO headquarters hub (MB2 850+ practices, Jefferson 60+, DECA/Ideal, MINT with a "MINT-owned dental lab," Community Dental Partners 70+, Apex Dental Partners 50+, Rodeo 50+), but MB2 runs lab spend through a Procurement Lab Manager who owns a "preferred lab strategy," and Leixir maintains an MB2 landing page and a Carrollton, TX center. A $140k/yr lab will not displace that in 12 months. South Florida's largest DSO is Sage Dental (Boca Raton, 150+ offices); its lab sourcing is unknown.

(5) Logistics and price. SEA-DFW: about 100 nonstops a week (American, Alaska, Delta), 4 hours, Kayak 12-month average round trip $392. SEA-MIA: 21-25 nonstops a week (one daily each on American, Alaska, Delta), about 6 hours, average round trip $438, 3-hour time difference. UPS 2026 list rates: 2nd Day Air 1 lb $45.75 (zone 7, Dallas) / $46.67 (zone 8, Miami); Ground $14.83 / $15.03 but 4-5 business days (zones are my estimate from mileage; fuel surcharge and account discounts not included). National labs already ship into both metros at $89-$122 for monolithic zirconia in 3 days (Crown World $89 digital, ROE zRc $93), so Integra's $129 dentist price is not an edge. Its lab-to-lab prices ($22 mill-only crown, $650 full-arch from STL, $299 ti-bar) are well below Mabel ($39-59 crown; $999 copy-mill to $1,999 full package) and ROE ($2,420 final arch), so the only credible wedge is selling idle 5-axis capacity to other labs, with $15-47 freight per case eroding it.

ESTIMATES. DFW: 2-5 obtainable accounts in 12 months, realistically 1-2 lab-to-lab milling customers among small DFW labs lacking wet 5-axis mills, plus 1-3 dentist accounts from personal or ARUM-dealer relationships; incremental revenue perhaps $1-4k/month, contingent on resolving TSBDE registration and the CDT requirement. The stronger DFW angle is the ARUM dealership (no territory restriction) into a lab-short metro, which can create captive milling and training customers. South Florida: 0-2 accounts and no structural reason to win: lab-dense, price-aggressive (a Hialeah lab itself cites $35-80 offshore crowns), same-day local service, thinnest flight schedule, and no existing relationships.

UNKNOWNS that matter: county-level CBP lab counts; whether TSBDE actually enforces registration on out-of-state labs; whether Integra has a CDT; latest county dentist counts; Sage Dental's lab sourcing; negotiated parcel discounts.

findings.claim: Texas requires a registration certificate to provide or offer dental laboratory services; statute applies to each lab 'doing business in this state' with no express out-of-state exemption
findings.detail: Tex. Occ. Code 266.151(b): a person may not operate or offer to operate a dental laboratory or provide or offer to provide dental laboratory services without a registration certificate. 266.153 requires an application for each laboratory 'doing business in this state.' 266.102(b)(5)(D)-(E) authorizes Board rules on referral of prescriptions to out-of-state labs and on devices manufactured out of state. 266.102(e): Board annually sends every Texas dentist the list of registered labs. Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: Texas-registered labs must employ a Certified Dental Technician on premises at least 30 hours/week
findings.detail: 22 TAC 116.5(a): all dental laboratories must have a CDT 'employed by and working on the premises of the dental laboratory a minimum of 30 hours per week'; exemptions only for dentist-owned on-premises labs (<3 technicians) and labs registered continuously since Sept 1, 1987. Material for Integra: unknown whether any Bellevue staff holds CDT. Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: TSBDE dental lab registration fee $125 initial; $136 annual renewal; renew by Dec 31; jurisprudence assessment every 3 years
findings.detail: From TSBDE 'Initial Dental Lab 2022' application PDF: 'FEE: $125'; renewal fee $136; late penalty one-half of initial fee. TSBDE's current fee-schedule page is JavaScript-only and did not render, so the 2022 figures are the best available and should be verified. Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: TSBDE's 'Do I Need a Dental Laboratory Registration in Texas' decision chart contains no exemption based on the lab's location
findings.detail: Chart exempts only dental students, dentist-owned on-premises labs serving own patients, and component manufacturers; anyone else making prosthetic appliances 'is required to hold a dental lab registration with the TSBDE.' Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: Texas CE rule: exempt labs' designated employee needs 12 CE hours/yr; otherwise proof the designated CDT maintains certification
findings.detail: 22 TAC 116.6(a)-(d); at least one regulatory-compliance course annually; max one business course; max 4 self-study hours. Accessed 2026-10-12.
findings.value: 12 CE hrs/yr (exempt labs) or current CDT

findings.claim: Texas-registered labs must label or certify whether a prosthesis was made entirely by them, by another domestic lab, or by a foreign lab (with country)
findings.detail: 22 TAC 116.10(f); relevant if a DFW lab outsources milling to Integra (domestic) - disclosure to the dentist is required. Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: Florida: out-of-state labs serving Florida dentists are not required to register
findings.detail: Fla. Stat. 466.032(5)(d)2: 'A dental laboratory in another state or country which provides service to a dentist licensed under this chapter is not required to register with the state and may continue to provide services to such dentist with a proper prescription... may voluntarily comply.' In-state labs register biennially, fee not to exceed $300; owner or one employee completes 18 CE hours biennially; $40 delinquency fee. Accessed 2026-10-12.
findings.value: exempt; in-state fee cap $300 biennial; 18 CE hrs

findings.claim: Florida Board of Dentistry dental laboratory registration application fee is $200 (non-refundable); rules in F.A.C. chapter 64B27
findings.detail: Board page lists Application Fee $200.00; application PDF 'Dental Laboratory Registration $200.00'; Rule 64B27-1.002 Dental Laboratory Biennial Registration (latest version effective 2021-06-13). Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: Texas exempts dental and prosthetic devices from sales and use tax
findings.detail: Tex. Tax Code 151.313(a)(5) exempts 'a brace; hearing aid or audio loop; orthopedic, dental, or prosthetic device... or supplies or replacement parts for the listed items.' Mirror text used because statutes.capitol.texas.gov Tax Code page is JS-rendered; mirror cites source accessed 2025-05-26. Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: Florida exempts dentures and prescription prosthetic appliances from sales tax
findings.detail: Fla. Stat. 212.08(2)(a): exempt 'dentures; hearing aids; crutches; prosthetic and orthopedic appliances'; (2)(b)1 defines prosthetic appliances and ties exemption to prescription by practitioners incl. ch. 466 dentists. Implemented by Rule 12A-1.021 (Prosthetic and Orthopedic Appliances), effective 2010-07-12. Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: Texas foreign LLC registration fee is $750
findings.detail: Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code 4.154 applies for-profit corporation fees to LLCs; 4.152(3): 'for filing an application of a foreign corporation for registration to transact business in this state, $750.' SOS site returned HTTP 403 to the crawler; statute mirror used. Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: Texas franchise tax: no tax due below $2,650,000 total revenue for 2026-2027 reports, but an annual Public Information Report is still required; $50 late-filing penalty
findings.detail: Comptroller page: 2026 and 2027 No Tax Due Threshold $2,650,000; rate 0.375% retail/wholesale, 0.75% other; report due May 15; '$50 penalty is assessed on each report filed after the due date.' Accessed 2026-10-12.
findings.value: $0 tax at Integra's scale; filing required

findings.claim: Florida foreign LLC qualification $125 ($100 filing + $25 registered agent); annual report $138.75 (due by May 1; $538.75 if late)
findings.detail: Sunbiz fee table: New Florida/Foreign LLC Filing Fee $100, Registered Agent Fee $25, Annual Report (with supplemental fee) $138.75, after May 1 $538.75. Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: Shipping finished prostheses into Texas or Florida from Washington, with no in-state employees or property, likely does not require foreign qualification
findings.detail: Estimate based on the general interstate-commerce exclusions in state 'transacting business' statutes (e.g., Tex. BOC ch. 9 list of activities not constituting transacting business); not fetched or verified in this research. Registration becomes necessary if Integra leases space or hires staff in-state. Verify with counsel.
findings.value: likely not required for ship-in sales

findings.claim: DFW dentist supply (official, 2020): Dallas 1,678; Tarrant 1,093; Collin 884; Denton 450 = 4,105 four-county
findings.detail: Texas DSHS HPRC 'Dentists by County - September 2020': Collin 85.1 per 100k (rank 2 statewide), Dallas 61.4, Tarrant 51.0, Denton 50.1. Newer years are on a Tableau dashboard that could not be read; 2022-2024 table URLs returned not-found/timeout. Accessed 2026-10-12.

Specialists: Broward 445, Miami-Dade 429, Palm Beach 343 (prosthodontists 49/47/47). The 2023-2024 report PDF exists (uploaded 2026-02) but did not parse. Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: Directory-based practice counts (not dentists) for context, 2026
findings.detail: dental.me directory: Dallas County 2,095 practice records; Tarrant 1,614; Collin 1,237; Denton 709; Miami-Dade 1,755; Broward 1,245; Palm Beach 959. Groundwork (citing CBP 2023) shows 1,543 payroll establishments classed as offices of dentists in Miami-Dade, up 13% from 2019. These are listings/establishments, not licensed dentists. Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: State-level dental lab establishments (CBP 2023, NAICS 339116): Florida 424 (2,569 employees), Texas 277 (2,406), Washington 175 (1,142); U.S. 4,782
findings.detail: Two independent secondary tabulations of Census County Business Patterns 2023 (PlainBizBench and Fair Market Value) agree. Florida ranks #2 nationally by establishments despite having fewer dentists than Texas - South Florida is lab-dense. County-level 339116 counts require a Census API key and could not be retrieved. Accessed 2026-10-12.
findings.value: FL 424 vs TX 277 vs WA 175 establishments

findings.claim: Directory count of dental labs in Florida: 847 statewide; Miami 97, Hialeah 42, Fort Lauderdale 19, Sunrise 17, West Palm Beach 16 (named cities only)
findings.detail: poidata.io Google-listing scrape, June 2026; counts include some dentist offices and duplicates and exclude labs in unnamed cities, so tri-county total is understated at 191+. Accessed 2026-10-12.
findings.value: >=191 listed labs in Miami-Dade/Broward/Palm Beach cities

findings.claim: The same directory's Texas count (249 statewide; Dallas 8) is inconsistent with CBP (277 payroll labs) and under-counts DFW
findings.detail: poidata.io Texas page (Aug 2025) lists El Paso 22, Houston 14, Dallas 8; this research alone identified 10+ DFW labs by website, so the Texas directory figure is unreliable and is not used for density. Accessed 2026-10-12.
findings.value: DFW lab count: not reliably countable from directories

findings.claim: Lab-technician supply: Miami metro has far higher concentration (LQ 1.31) than DFW (LQ 0.75); Texas statewide LQ 0.57 vs Florida 1.12 (OEWS May 2023)
findings.detail: BLS OEWS May 2023 occupation profile 51-9081: Miami-Fort Lauderdale-West Palm Beach 800 employed, 0.30 per 1,000 jobs, LQ 1.31, mean $26.65/hr ($55,430); Dallas-Fort Worth-Arlington 670, LQ 0.75, mean $23.82 ($49,550); Seattle-Tacoma-Bellevue 550, LQ 1.17, mean $29.16 ($60,640); Florida 2,410 employed LQ 1.12 ($26.05); Texas 1,750 LQ 0.57 ($23.35). National mean $25.19, median $22.93. Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: DFW dental lab technician wages, OEWS May 2025: median $23.08/hr ($48,010); mean $25.27/hr ($52,550); employment 610
findings.detail: Mirror of BLS May 2025 metro estimates (txlaborintel.com): 10th pct $16.50, 25th $17.00, 75th $31.05, 90th $35.99. Bellevue comparison: Seattle metro mean $29.16 (May 2023), i.e., DFW techs cost roughly 15-20% less than Seattle. Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: Miami metro dental lab technician wages, OEWS May 2025: median $59,940/yr; employment 590 (secondary mirror); estimates for this metro swing widely year to year
findings.detail: WageDex (compiling BLS May 2025) ranks Miami-Fort Lauderdale-West Palm Beach #17 by median at $59,940 (employment 590). Prior BLS releases: May 2022 1,040 employed at $22.70 mean; May 2023 800 at $26.65 mean. Treat Miami tech wages as roughly $23-29/hr with high sampling variance. Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: Most DFW full-arch/All-on-X centers operate in-house labs, limiting them to overflow or component (ti-bar) targets
findings.detail: Advanced Dentistry, Lewisville ('on-site lab... final teeth made under our roof'; same-day from $10,500/arch); ARCHPOINT Implant Dentistry, Dallas/Southlake/Fort Worth ('On-Site State-of-the-Art Lab'); Texas Implant & Dental Center, Fort Worth (surgery suite + dental lab + restorative in one location; 3-4 cases/week); Forte Implant Center, Plano ('in-house laboratory', $15,500 nano-ceramic / $19,500 zirconia per arch); The Dental Implant Place, Fort Worth ('98% of all implant prosthetics... made in-house', CAD + 3D milling); Innate Dental Solutions, Plano ('laboratory is in the building'; fixed full arch $13,000/arch); Dallas All on 4 Dental Implant Center, Irving ('full in-house lab'; single arch from $9,500, zirconia full mouth $24,400). Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: DFW full-arch centers that disclose using outside/partner labs or no in-house lab: 10 Day Smiles (Arlington/Coppell) and R. David Brumbaugh DDS (Dallas)
findings.detail: 10 Day Smiles: 'Our in-house and partner labs...'; All-on-4 $9,995/arch; digital planning. Brumbaugh: single-provider All-on-4 with CBCT, no in-house lab mentioned. These are the realistic DFW full-arch lab prospects. Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: Most South Florida full-arch centers also run in-house labs, including the chains
findings.detail: Nuvia Dental Implant Center Miami (6262 Sunset Dr): 'Teeth Created By In-House Lab', permanent zirconia in 24 hours. OneSolution Dental Implant Centers (Miami + S FL): 'state-of-the-art digital lab... on-site technicians, not outsourced'. Done In One (Boca Raton): in-house lab, zirconia final in one week. In A Day Smile (Fort Lauderdale): in-house lab with 3Shape scanners, 3D printing, three lab techs, in-house milling. Smiland Dental (Fort Lauderdale): in-house lab technician, zirconia finals. Boca Dental (Boca Raton): in-house lab, PiC photogrammetry, X-Nav. Art Dental Studio (Hialeah/Kendall/Cooper City): in-house master ceramist. Accessed 2026-10-12.
findings.source_date: 2025-12-05 (In A Day Smile post); others undated
findings.value: 7 of 9 named S FL centers in-house

findings.claim: South Florida full-arch practices without a disclosed in-house lab: ADW Center and DG Dental, both Fort Lauderdale
findings.detail: ADW Center (Dr. Boris Lipovetskiy): All-on-4 from $13,999/arch incl. CBCT and PRP; zirconia finals; no lab mentioned. DG Dental (Dr. Dory Green): same-day temporaries, porcelain/zirconia finals; no lab mentioned. Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: MB2 Dental (Carrollton, TX) supports 850+ practices and centralizes lab purchasing under a Procurement Lab Manager who owns the 'preferred lab strategy'
findings.detail: MB2 job posting (Sept 2026): 'Procurement Lab Manager... own and lead our laboratory category strategy... manage lab spend, relationships, contracts, performance... preferred lab strategy to drive savings, quality, service, and doctor adoption.' MB2 HQ 2403 Lacy Lane, Carrollton, TX 75006; partners typically have >$1.25M revenue and 5+ ops. Implication: lab access is via corporate procurement, not individual office outreach. Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: Leixir Dental Laboratory Group maintains an MB2-specific landing page and a Texas 'Global Center of Excellence' (Care 1st Dental Institute) in Carrollton, TX, with a DSO lab program
findings.detail: leixir.com/mb2/ offers MB2 practices a 'global lab partner'; leixir.com/service-area/texas/ describes the Carrollton education/center and service to Dallas, Fort Worth, Plano, Arlington; DSO page cites 15+ years with large DSOs. This is the incumbent for DFW DSO lab spend. Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.detail: MINT recruiting PDF: 'DIGITAL IMPRESSIONS USING INTRAORAL SCANNERS; MINT OWNED DENTAL LAB WHERE WE CONTROL THE QUALITY.' A captive DSO lab is a possible ARUM mill or overflow-milling prospect rather than a lab-services account. Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.detail: ROE Fee Schedule 2026 (rev 10/07/26): zRc zirconia $93 model-free 3 days; TLZ with MiYO $122; e.max monolithic $134; TLZ-SR screw-retained implant crown $299; TLZ-IB full-arch zirconia final $2,420 (10 days); NobelProcera $2,888; analog full-arch package (5 implants) $4,309. Integra's dentist price ($129 FCZ, $149 e.max) is at or above these. Accessed 2026-10-12.

findings.claim: SEA-MIA: only 21-25 nonstops per week (one daily each on American AA1471, Alaska AS305, Delta DL506), 5h39m-6h13m, 2,721-2,736 miles; average round trip ~$438 (Kayak 12-month), range $343-$572
findings.detail: 2LNR (schedule confirmed 2026-10-04): 21 nonstops/week; FlightsFrom: 21/week, approx RT $400 (monthly $246-$686); Directflights (updated 2026-09-28): 25 weekly incl. AA 11/week; Kayak: 3-4/day, 12-month average $438; Alaska Saver one-way from $214-$249. Three-hour time difference vs two for Dallas. Accessed 2026-10-12.

Whether TSBDE in practice requires or enforces registration for out-of-state laboratories that ship to Texas dentists; the statute and TSBDE chart contain no exemption, but no enforcement record or Board FAQ on out-of-state labs was found.
Whether any Integra employee holds CDT certification (required on-premises 30 hrs/week under 22 TAC 116.5 if Integra registers in Texas).
Current (FY2026) TSBDE dental laboratory fees; the fee-schedule page is JavaScript-only and did not render, so 2022 application figures ($125/$136) are used.

Most recent official county dentist counts: Texas DSHS 2022-2024 county supply tables are on a Tableau dashboard that could not be read; the Florida DOH 2023-2024 dentist workforce PDF (uploaded Feb 2026) did not parse. ADA HPI county-level counts were not retrieved.
Sage Dental's (and Dental Care Alliance's) laboratory sourcing model and whether any South Florida DSO operates a captive lab.
Terms and incumbents of DSO lab contracts in DFW (MB2's preferred labs beyond the Leixir landing page; Jefferson, DECA/Ideal, CDP, Apex Dental Partners, Rodeo sourcing).
ClearChoice DFW and South Florida centers' lab arrangement (ClearChoice Fort Lauderdale page confirmed; in-center lab status not verified in this research).
Exact UPS/FedEx zones from ZIP 98007 to Dallas/Miami ZIPs, applicable fuel surcharge, and Integra's negotiated discount; FedEx list rates could not be fetched (fedex.com blocks crawlers).
Whether milling/lab capacity actually constrains any specific DFW lab (the lab-to-lab thesis assumes some small DFW labs lack wet 5-axis mills; no lab publicly states this).
Spanish-language service expectations and referral networks in Miami-Dade dentistry (not researched; could matter for a remote English-only lab).

Whether shipping finished prostheses into TX/FL without staff or property triggers foreign-qualification or franchise-tax nexus (statutory interstate-commerce exclusions not fetched; verify with counsel).
